reply.subject: RSW_Shiro

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: an olive-green reptile seen face-on. Its fan of tall, curling, ridged shell plates frames a broad head with two small red eyes on top. It stands on four thick, wrinkled, grey-olive columnar legs. East: a long side profile. The body stands high on four elephant-like legs under a high crest of backswept wavy plates. A long horizontal neck with stripes ends in a flat duck-billed snout with raised red eyes. A long, level tail with a row of small spikes runs behind. North: the rear view. The shell plates stack into a tall triangular, pine-tree-like peak, and a knobbed neck or head stub with two small bumps pokes above the top. A short spiked tail stub hangs down the centre between the hind legs. The feet share a ground line, but north's top sits clearly higher than south's.
observed.south.png: A front view at full resolution. The face is toward the camera: a wide, flat snout seen nearly end-on, two raised red eyes, and a broad mouth line. A fan of ridged, curled olive plates with yellow-green highlights rises behind the head. Four columnar wrinkled legs with blunt toes. Painterly and detailed. The face reads slightly friendly and rounded but not glossy-eyed. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right. A high domed carapace of overlapping backswept ridged plates ends in blunt wavy spines, like a crest along the back. Long horizontal neck with yellow-green and olive stripes, and a long duck-billed snout with small red eyes on top. A long level tail with small dorsal spikes. Four thick, wrinkled, greyer legs hold the body well clear of the ground. Realistic painterly rendering, no outlines. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: A rear view. Ridged shell plates with wavy spine tips stack into a steep triangular peak. A segmented knob with two small rounded bumps (no eye surfaces) sticks up above the peak. A short tail with a ridge of small bumps hangs down the centre over the haunches. Two thick hind legs in front and two forelegs behind them, all wrinkled grey. No face or eyes visible. Clean alpha. The shell silhouette is noticeably taller and more pointed than in the south view.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the Shiro stands beside the vanilla human, about 1.5 cells long and a bit lower than the human's head height: a large, low beast. At 32 px/cell it reads as a spiky olive mound on legs, larger than the rat, distinct from the ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head face-on with two red eyes and the snout toward the camera, with the shell fan behind.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the shell's back, the hanging tail and the hind legs. The knob above the peak has bumps but no eye surfaces, and there is no face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three views are at the low game angle with the legs visible; none is overhead.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 23%. Leg and foot sizes match across facings, but north's shell peak plus the head knob rise well above the south crest (in facings.png the north top is at about y=100 vs south at about y=160). It is mostly a silhouette difference, not a pose.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same palette, legs and plate style. But the shell outline differs: a wide fan on south, a tall narrow pyramid on north. Also, the head sits low at the front on a horizontal neck (east, south), yet on north a neck or head knob rises above the top of the shell, which that neck could not do.

SIGNATURE.seen: The spiny, ridged shell, which defines the animal, dominates every facing.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1. Spines on the shell: present. The blunt wavy spine tips end every plate on all facings, plus spikes on the tail.

CANON.seen: High columnar elephant-like wrinkled legs with the body clear of the ground: yes. High domed carapace of backswept ridged plates with blunt wavy spines: yes. Long duck-billed snout with small raised red eyes: yes (east). Long level tail with small spikes: yes (east). Olive-moss shell, yellow-green highlights, striped neck, greyer legs: yes. Realistic, no outlines: yes. Not a turtle, toy or shiro-trap: yes.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, with natural horn texture and wrinkled hide. The south face is slightly rounded and friendly but not cartoon.

OURS.seen: A bespoke painterly render matching the canon reference, not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: No backdrop, ground patch or shadow on any facing.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Redrawn painterly off the canon reference, as the 2026-10-31 card asked.

SCALE.seen: About 1.5 cells long, a little shorter than a human. That fits a large, slow pack-reptile; the description gives no size words.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a spiky olive body on legs, apart from the ground.

reply.image_seen: The montage and three individual facings show an olive, plated quadruped with wrinkled columnar legs, a broad frontal bill, an extended side-profile neck and tail, and a rear-facing head beyond the shell; the scale panel shows it beside a human and rat.

concerns.evidence: North shows a broad scalloped shell base narrowing toward the distant neck, with overlapping ridged plates receding along the back. The paired knobs belong to the rear of the distant head, whose neck projects upscreen with depth. The central tail points downscreen between the nearer haunches. These features support a rear view of the long-bodied animal shown in east.

The measured 23% height spread includes the distant head extending above north's shell. North's thick foreground legs and broad shell base remain comparable in scale to south. East exposes the long horizontal neck and tail that project along the screen's vertical direction when the animal turns north, accounting for the taller silhouette.

South's mouth corners curve slightly upward, but the bill has dense horizontal skin folds, a heavy flattened shape and restrained natural shading. The small red eyes sit within textured brow ridges. The visible facial treatment supports realistic reptile anatomy.
